local_calendar.t: On November 3, 2026 each Illinois county elects its county clerk, treasurer and sheriff and the county board members whose terms are ending; Cook County also elects its board president, its assessor and members of its Board of Review. On the same ballot are the regional superintendents of schools, the commissioners of the Metropolitan Water Reclamation District and elected trustees of other sanitary districts, the Chicago Board of Education, and circuit judges, both to fill vacancies and on the question of retention; state's attorneys, circuit clerks, coroners and county auditors are elected in presidential years, next in 2028. Cities, villages, townships, park, library, fire protection and community college districts and the other school boards are elected, with few exceptions, at the consolidated election on the first Tuesday in April of odd-numbered years, next in 2027.
local_calendar.s: Illinois Election Code, 10 ILCS 5/2A-1.1 and 2A-1.2 (which offices are filled at which election) and 2A-14 through 2A-23 (the years each county office is elected)

local_coverage.t: Illinois has no statewide list of county candidates: each of its election authorities publishes its own. Loaded here from the State Board of Elections' candidate list: the regional superintendents of schools of the 24 regions of more than one county and the circuit judges (53 vacancies and 128 retention questions), 212 candidates. From the Cook County Clerk's list, in the order of its ballot numbers: Cook County's own offices (24 contests: the board president, clerk, sheriff, treasurer, assessor, 17 commissioners and 2 Board of Review seats), the Metropolitan Water Reclamation District, 3 suburban sanitary districts and the regional superintendents of 3 neighbouring one-county regions (these without an order: the Clerk's ballot numbers are those of Cook County's own ballots), 55 candidates. From the Chicago Board of Election Commissioners' list, which the Board calls unofficial while filings can still change: the Chicago Board of Education (21 contests, 42 candidates). Left out: ballot questions; write-in candidates (the Chicago list marks 30 contests with a write-in line and names no one); 2 judges who withdrew from retention; and the county offices of the other 101 counties, each named among the gaps. The State Board's list is not in ballot order, so no order is given for its contests.
